mainTopic: Loaves of a תודה slaughtered with a flaw, the רבא–רבה dispute about a חטאת, and when נסכים become holy
overview: The amud continues the ברייתא about the forty loaves of a תודה: does slaughtering the animal make them holy when something is wrong with the slaughter? רבי מאיר says רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about a בעל מום. רבי יהודה says everyone agrees about טריפה, חוץ לזמנו and בעל מום, and the argument is only about חוץ למקומו. רבי אליעזר compares that case to חוץ לזמנו, since both are about wrong intention. רבי יהושע compares it to בעל מום, since neither carries כרת, and then points to שלא לשמו, which matches on both features, so רבי אליעזר falls silent. The גמרא explains רבי מאיר's version as a minor eye blemish, following רבי עקיבא. It then ties a dispute between רבא and רבה about a חטאת slaughtered חוץ למקומה to this debate, giving two versions of whether רבה changed his mind. After a short note on why the משנה mentions the איל המילואים, a new משנה deals with נסכים whose זבח turned out פסול. The גמרא uses that משנה to test זעירי's rule that נסכים become holy only at the slaughter, and defends the rule.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's version: the dispute is about a blemished animal
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי מאיר, רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about a תודה that was slaughtered and then found to be a בעל מום. Do its loaves become holy?
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone slaughtered the thanks offering and it turned out to be blemished, רבי אליעזר says the loaves became holy and רבי יהושע says they did not. This is how רבי מאיר reports it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells us רבי מאיר's version of the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. In his version, the case is a blemished animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loaves of a תודה normally become holy when the animal is slaughtered. Here the animal turns out to be a בעל מום, so it is פסול. רבי אליעזר holds the slaughter still makes the loaves holy, and רבי יהושע holds it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering the offering, which is the act that makes the loaves holy
An animal with a blemish, which cannot be brought as a קרבן
Became holy. Here it refers to the loaves of the תודה
The forty loaves brought together with a thanks offering

phrases.english: If he slaughtered it and it was found to be blemished,
phrases.notes: "It" is the תודה, the thanks offering.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: it became holy,
phrases.notes: What became holy is the bread, the loaves that come with the תודה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: it did not become holy,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא connected to the משנה about the loaves of the תודה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, רבי אליעזר holds the loaves become holy when the slaughtered תודה is found to be a בעל מום, and רבי יהושע holds they do not.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's version: they argue only about intent outside its area
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the two sages agree about טריפה (not holy), חוץ לזמנו (holy) and בעל מום (not holy). Their only argument is about חוץ למקומו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע did not argue about a תודה that turned out to be a טריפה; both agree the loaves are not holy. They did not argue about intent to eat it after its time; both agree the loaves are holy. They did not argue about a blemished animal; both agree the loaves are not holy. So what did they argue about? Intent to eat it outside its proper area. רבי אליעזר says the loaves are holy, and רבי יהושע says they are not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a different report of the argument. He lists three cases where everyone agrees, and then names the one case they really argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי מאיר's version the argument was about בעל מום. רבי יהודה moves it: everyone agrees a בעל מום does not make the loaves holy. The real argument is about slaughtering with the intent to eat it חוץ למקומו, outside the proper place.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not argue. This introduces cases where everyone agrees
An animal with a fatal defect, which makes it invalid
Slaughtering with the intent to eat it (or burn its parts) after its allowed time
Slaughtering with the intent to eat it (or burn its parts) outside its allowed place

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. For רבי מאיר, the argument is about בעל מום. For רבי יהודה, everyone agrees about בעל מום (not holy), and the argument is only about חוץ למקומו.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the ברייתא is built on רבי יהודה's version. The three cases everyone agrees on become the models that each sage compares to.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua did not disagree
about where he slaughtered it and it was found to be a tereifa,
that it did not become holy,
and about intent beyond its time, that it became holy,
phrases.notes: This means he slaughtered it while planning to eat it after the time it may be eaten.

phrases.english: and about a blemished animal, that it did not become holy.
And about what did they disagree?
About intent outside its area,
for Rabbi Eliezer says: it became holy,
and Rabbi Yehoshua says: it did not become holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different report of where the same מחלוקת applies
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees: טריפה and בעל מום do not make the loaves holy, and חוץ לזמנו does. The argument is only about חוץ למקומו.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר compares 'outside its area' to 'beyond its time'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר argues that חוץ למקומו is like חוץ לזמנו, since both disqualify the offering. So just as חוץ לזמנו makes the loaves holy, חוץ למקומו does too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: Intent beyond its time disqualifies the offering, and intent outside its area also disqualifies it. So just as with beyond its time the loaves become holy, with outside its area they also become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר supports his view. He compares the disputed case to a case everyone agrees on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both חוץ לזמנו and חוץ למקומו are problems of wrong intent during the slaughter, and both make the offering פסול. Since everyone agrees the loaves become holy with חוץ לזמנו, רבי אליעזר says the same should be true for חוץ למקומו.

keyTerms.meaning: Since. It introduces the shared feature that the comparison is built on
Disqualified, invalid as an offering
Just as ... so too. The standard form for a comparison

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:
Since intent beyond its time is disqualified,
and intent outside its area is disqualified,
just as with beyond its time, it became holy,
so too with outside its area, it became holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: הוֹאִיל וְחוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי אליעזר's reason within רבי יהודה's version
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's ruling that חוץ למקומו makes the loaves holy
steps.raayaSupportSource: Comparison to חוץ לזמנו, where everyone agrees the loaves become holy

steps.title: רבי יהושע compares 'outside its area' to a blemished animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע argues that חוץ למקומו is like בעל מום, since both disqualify the offering. So just as a בעל מום does not make the loaves holy, neither does חוץ למקומו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: Intent outside its area disqualifies the offering, and a blemish also disqualifies it. So just as with a blemished animal the loaves do not become holy, with outside its area they also do not become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers with his own comparison. He uses the same kind of reasoning but links the disputed case to a different agreed case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע uses the same 'both are פסול' logic but picks בעל מום, where everyone agrees the loaves are not holy. Now there are two comparisons that pull in opposite directions, and that sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemished animal. Everyone agrees it does not make the loaves holy

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said:
Since intent outside its area is disqualified,
and a blemished animal is disqualified,
just as with a blemished animal, it did not become holy,
so too with outside its area, it did not become holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: הוֹאִיל וְחוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an opposing comparison to רבי אליעזר's
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע's ruling that חוץ למקומו does not make the loaves holy
steps.raayaSupportSource: Comparison to בעל מום, where everyone agrees the loaves do not become holy

steps.title: רבי אליעזר proposes testing which comparison fits better
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר points out that each of them made a different comparison. He suggests they check which case חוץ למקומו is really more similar to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: I compared it to beyond its time, and you compared it to a blemished animal. Let us see which one it is more like. If it is like beyond its time, we will learn its law from beyond its time. If it is like a blemished animal, we will learn its law from a blemished animal.
steps.whatsHappening: Both sides made a comparison, so רבי אליעזר suggests a way to decide between them. This is a setup line: the next part of the ברייתא will check which case is truly more similar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison only works if the two cases are really alike. Since both comparisons are built on 'it is פסול,' רבי אליעזר wants to find a closer point of similarity to decide which model wins.

keyTerms.meaning: I compared it (to another case)
Let us see which one it resembles
We will judge it, meaning we will learn its law from that case

steps.whatToRemember: In רבי יהודה's version, everyone agrees on three cases: טריפה (not holy), חוץ לזמנו (holy) and בעל מום (not holy). The argument is about חוץ למקומו. רבי אליעזר compares it to חוץ לזמנו, רבי יהושע compares it to בעל מום, and now they will test which comparison is closer.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
I compared it to intent beyond its time,
and you compared it to a blemished animal,
let us see to which it is similar:

phrases.aramaic: אִם דּוֹמֶה לְחוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ, נְדוּנֶנּוּ מֵחוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ,
phrases.english: if it is similar to beyond its time, we will judge it from beyond its time;

phrases.aramaic: אִם דּוֹמֶה לְבַעַל מוּם, נְדוּנֶנּוּ מִבַּעַל מוּם.
phrases.english: if it is similar to a blemished animal, we will judge it from a blemished animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: אֲנִי דִּמִּיתִיהוּ לְחוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the clash between the two comparisons by proposing a test of similarity
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is חוץ למקומו closer to חוץ לזמנו or to בעל מום?

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: compare intention to intention, not to a body defect
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר argues that חוץ למקומו is a problem of wrong intention, so it should be learned from חוץ לזמנו, which is also wrong intention. It should not be learned from בעל מום, which is a physical defect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר began to argue: We learn a disqualification caused by thought from another disqualification caused by thought. We do not learn a disqualification caused by thought from a disqualification in the animal's body.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers his own question from step 5. He picks which comparison is the better one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חוץ למקומו and חוץ לזמנו both come from what the person was thinking during the service. A בעל מום is a flaw in the animal itself. So רבי אליעזר says the closer match is חוץ לזמנו, and that would make the loaves holy.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn one case from another (by comparing them)
A disqualification caused by wrong thought or intention during the service
A disqualification in the animal's body itself, like a blemish

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer began to reason:
We learn a disqualification of intention
from a disqualification of intention,
phrases.notes: He means: learn חוץ למקומו from חוץ לזמנו, since both are about what the person intended.

phrases.english: and we do not learn a disqualification of intention
from a disqualification of the body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 5 from רבי אליעזר's side
steps.raayaObject: Loaves of a תודה slaughtered חוץ למקומו become holy
steps.raayaSupportSource: Comparing kinds of disqualification: intention is matched with intention (חוץ לזמנו)

steps.title: רבי יהושע: compare by whether there is כרת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע argues that the right comparison is about כרת. חוץ למקומו carries no כרת, like בעל מום. חוץ לזמנו does carry כרת, so it is not a good comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע began to argue: We learn a disqualification that has no כרת from another disqualification that has no כרת. חוץ לזמנו cannot be the proof, because it is a disqualification that does have כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע offers a different way to decide which case is more similar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע says the important feature is the punishment of כרת, not whether the problem came from thought or from the body. Since חוץ לזמנו carries כרת and חוץ למקומו does not, they are not truly alike. That leaves בעל מום as the match, so the loaves are not holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Being cut off spiritually; a heavenly punishment
Let it not serve as proof

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua began to reason:
We learn a disqualification that has no karet
from a disqualification that has no karet,
and beyond its time should not serve as proof,
since it is a disqualification that has karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אליעזר's comparison with a different measure of similarity
steps.raayaObject: Loaves of a תודה slaughtered חוץ למקומו do not become holy
steps.raayaSupportSource: Comparing kinds of disqualification by whether they carry כרת (matched with בעל מום)

steps.title: רבי יהושע: even by your measure, שלא לשמו is the better match
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע adds a second point. Even if we compare intention to intention, as רבי אליעזר wants, there is a closer case: שלא לשמו. It is a disqualification of intention, and it also has no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also: let us learn it from שלא לשמו, which is a disqualification of intention and has no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע beats רבי אליעזר's argument using רבי אליעזר's own rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלא לשמו matches חוץ למקומו on both features: it comes from intention, and it has no כרת. So it is a better match than חוץ לזמנו. In the case of שלא לשמו the loaves do not become holy, so the same should be true for חוץ למקומו.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; an extra argument
Slaughtering the offering with the intention that it is a different kind of offering

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a classic way to win an argument: accept your opponent's standard, and then find a case that fits it even better.

phrases.english: And furthermore, let us learn it from 'not for its sake,'
since it is a disqualification of intention
and it has no karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second argument that works even within רבי אליעזר's own standard
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי אליעזר's choice of חוץ לזמנו as the case to compare with
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is a closer intention-based case (שלא לשמו) that also matches on having no כרת

steps.title: רבי אליעזר is silent
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר does not answer, which shows that he accepts רבי יהושע's argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: The debate ends. רבי אליעזר has no reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His silence means he concedes. רבי יהושע's comparisons stand, so in רבי יהודה's version a תודה slaughtered with intent חוץ למקומו does not make the loaves holy.

keyTerms.meaning: And he was silent (a sign that he gave in)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר compared by intention (חוץ לזמנו). רבי יהושע compared by כרת (בעל מום). רבי יהושע then pointed to שלא לשמו, which matches both ways, and רבי אליעזר was silent.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer was silent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the debate with רבי אליעזר conceding
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהושע's argument wins: חוץ למקומו is compared to cases with no כרת, so the loaves are not holy

steps.title: Question on רבי מאיר: why is טריפה different from בעל מום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about רבי מאיר's version. Why is a טריפה treated as a problem that existed before slaughter, while a בעל מום is not?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי מאיר: why is it different when he slaughtered it and it turned out to be a טריפה, so that its problem counts as existing before the slaughter? And why is it different when he slaughtered it and it turned out to be a בעל מום, so that its problem does not count as existing before the slaughter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי מאיר's version from step 1 and challenges a difference it seems to make.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי מאיר's version, everyone agrees that a טריפה does not make the loaves holy, but רבי אליעזר holds that a בעל מום does. Both problems seem to have been there before the slaughter. So the גמרא wants to know why they would be treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? (asking for a reason to treat two cases differently)
Its disqualification existed before the slaughter
An animal with a fatal internal defect

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir,
what is different when he slaughtered it and it was found to be a tereifa,
that its disqualification counts as before slaughter,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי שְׁנָא שְׁחָטָהּ וְנִמְצֵאת בַּעֲלַת מוּם,
phrases.english: and what is different when he slaughtered it and it was found to be blemished,
that its disqualification does not count as before slaughter?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, מַאי שְׁנָא שְׁחָטָהּ וְנִמְצֵאת טְרֵיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבי יהודה's version and returns to רבי מאיר's version to challenge it
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's version, in which טריפה and בעל מום are treated differently
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both defects were present before the slaughter, so there seems to be no reason why only one of them stops the loaves from becoming holy

steps.title: The blemish is a small eye blemish, following רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר is talking about דוקין שבעין. רבי עקיבא holds that an animal with such a blemish is not taken down once it is on the מזבח, so it is partly valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about a blemish on the cornea of the eye. This follows רבי עקיבא, who said: if such animals went up onto the מזבח, they are not taken down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 10. The בעל מום in רבי מאיר's version is a minor eye blemish, which is not a full disqualification.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טריפה is fully disqualified, so it cannot make the לחם holy. But according to רבי עקיבא, an animal with דוקין שבעין stays on the מזבח once it has gone up. So it is valid enough after the fact to make the לחם holy.

keyTerms.meaning: A small blemish on the cornea of the eye, a minor kind of מום
If they went up onto the מזבח, they are not taken down. The offering is accepted after the fact.
According to the view of

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that not every מום is the same. A minor blemish can still count after the fact, while a טריפה cannot.

phrases.english: With a blemish on the cornea of the eye,
and according to Rabbi Akiva,
who said: if they went up, they shall not come down.
phrases.notes: Going up means the animal was already placed on the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a specific type of מום, following a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any בעל מום is fully disqualified, just like a טריפה, so it should not make the לחם holy
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is דוקין שבעין. According to רבי עקיבא it stays on the מזבח once it has gone up, so it can make the לחם holy.

steps.title: רבי יהושע limits רבי עקיבא's rule to the animal itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע explains that רבי עקיבא's rule only keeps the animal on the מזבח. It does not make the לחם holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע would say: when רבי עקיבא said 'if they went up they are not taken down,' he meant only the disqualification of the animal itself. But for making the bread holy, he did not say this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יהושע does not accept this answer. In his view, a blemished animal still does not make the לחם holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע agrees with רבי עקיבא's rule but limits how far it reaches. 'Not taken down' only protects the offering that is already on the מזבח. It does not turn the slaughter into a valid act for making the לחם holy.

keyTerms.meaning: The disqualification of the offering itself
To make the loaves of the תודה holy through the slaughter

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע is not arguing with רבי עקיבא's rule. He accepts it and only limits it to the animal itself.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua would say:
When Rabbi Akiva said
'if they went up, they shall not come down,'
that was about the disqualification of the offering itself,
but for making the bread holy, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: כִּי אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי יהושע would respond to the answer given in Step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the reach of a rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If רבי עקיבא's rule makes the animal valid after the fact, it should also make the לחם holy
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule only keeps the animal on the מזבח. It does not make the לחם holy.

steps.title: רבא and רבה argue about a חטאת slaughtered with intent outside its place
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that a חטאת slaughtered with intent חוץ לזמנה is not taken down once it is on the מזבח. For חוץ למקומה, רבא says it is taken down, and רבה says it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: a חטאת that was slaughtered with intent to eat it after its time is not taken down if it went up onto the מזבח. If the intent was to eat it outside its place, רבא says it is taken down, and רבה says it is not taken down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new dispute between אמוראים. It sets up a link back to the argument of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of חוץ לזמנה is agreed on. The question is whether חוץ למקומה is like חוץ לזמנה, so it is not taken down, or more like a בעל מום, so it is taken down.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering
With intent to eat it after its permitted time
With intent to eat it outside its permitted area
It shall come down, meaning it is removed from the מזבח

phrases.english: It was stated:
A sin offering that one slaughtered with intent to eat it beyond its time,
if it went up, it shall not come down.
With intent to eat it outside its place:
Rava says: it shall come down,
phrases.notes: Coming down means it is taken off the מזבח and not burned there.

phrases.english: Rabba says: it shall not come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related dispute between אמוראים that will be tied to the earlier מחלוקת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חטאת slaughtered with intent חוץ לזמנה is not taken down. For חוץ למקומה, רבא says it is taken down and רבה says it is not.

steps.title: Linking רבא and רבה to רבי יהושע and רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבא follows רבי יהושע, and רבה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא holds like רבי יהושע, and רבה holds like רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the dispute of רבא and רבה to the earlier dispute of the תנאים. This sets up the final step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע compares חוץ למקומו to a בעל מום, and a blemished animal is taken down, so רבא says the חטאת is taken down. רבי אליעזר compares it to חוץ לזמנו, which is not taken down, so רבה says it is not taken down.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with the view of

phrases.english: Rava holds like Rabbi Yehoshua,
and Rabba holds like Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, וְרַבָּה כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the dispute in Step 13 to the dispute of the תנאים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא's view follows רבי יהושע's comparison to a בעל מום. רבה's view follows רבי אליעזר's comparison to חוץ לזמנו.

steps.title: רבה changes his mind and agrees with רבא
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי אליעזר accepted רבי יהושע's argument, רבה also gave up his view and agreed with רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה changed his mind and agreed with רבא, because רבי אליעזר changed his mind and agreed with רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that רבה went back on his view. In the end, a חטאת slaughtered with intent חוץ למקומה is taken down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's view depended on רבי אליעזר's comparison. Step 9 showed that רבי אליעזר accepted רבי יהושע's argument by staying silent. Once that support is gone, רבה's view has nothing to stand on, so he agrees with רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back on his view and changed his mind
Over to the side of someone's view

steps.whatToRemember: In this first version, חוץ למקומו is compared to a בעל מום, not to חוץ לזמנו. So a חטאת slaughtered with intent חוץ למקומה is taken down from the מזבח, and רבה comes to agree with רבא. The next step gives another version in which רבה keeps his view.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how an אמורא's view can fall away when the תנא it depends on changes his mind.

phrases.english: And Rabba retracted in favor of Rava,

phrases.aramaic: מִדַּהֲדַר בֵּיהּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְגַבֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
phrases.english: since Rabbi Eliezer retracted in favor of Rabbi Yehoshua.
phrases.notes: This points back to Step 9, where רבי אליעזר stayed silent and so accepted רבי יהושע's argument.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final result from the link made in Step 14 and the silence in Step 9
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to this version, רבה retracts and agrees with רבא, following רבי יהושע: a חטאת slaughtered with intent חוץ למקומה is taken down from the מזבח. Step 16 brings a version where רבה does not retract.

steps.title: A second version: רבה did not give up his view
steps.stepSummary: Some say רבה kept his view, because the argument that convinced רבי אליעזר does not work for a חטאת slaughtered חוץ למקומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: even though רבי אליעזר gave in to רבי יהושע, רבה did not give in to רבא. In the case of the לחם, רבי יהושע convinced him by saying, 'Let us learn it from an offering slaughtered שלא לשמו.' But here, if you learn it from שלא לשמו, the rule would be: once it is on the מזבח, it is not taken down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another version of the conclusion from step 15: רבה did not give in to רבא. It also explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע won by comparing the case to an offering slaughtered שלא לשמו. If we use that same comparison for a חטאת slaughtered חוץ למקומה, it actually supports רבה. An offering slaughtered שלא לשמו is not taken down once it is on the מזבח, so the same should be true here.

keyTerms.meaning: He took back his opinion
Let us judge it, meaning learn its law by comparing it to another case
Slaughtered for the wrong type of offering
If it went up on the מזבח, it is not taken down

steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, רבה agreed with רבא. In this version, רבה keeps his view, because the comparison to שלא לשמו supports him for חוץ למקומה.
steps.confusionAlert: The same comparison, to an offering slaughtered שלא לשמו, gives opposite results in the two cases. For the לחם it means the bread is not made holy. For the מזבח it means the animal is not taken down.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דַּהֲדַר בֵּיהּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.english: Even though Rabbi Eliezer took back his view
in favor of Rabbi Yehoshua,

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה לְגַבֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא לָא הֲדַר בֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: Rabba did not take back his view in favor of Rava.
There, it was because he said to him:
phrases.notes: 'There' means the argument about the bread of the תודה, from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: Let us learn it from an offering slaughtered not for its sake,
But here,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the חטאת slaughtered with intent חוץ למקומה.

phrases.english: if you learn it from an offering slaughtered not for its sake,
then if it went up, it does not come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of step 15's conclusion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה did not give in. The comparison to שלא לשמו supports 'אם עלתה לא תרד' for a חטאת slaughtered חוץ למקומה.

steps.title: Why does the משנה mention איל המילואים and not איל נזיר?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks why the משנה picked the inauguration ram instead of the common nazir's ram.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said, 'If he slaughtered it שלא לשמה,' and so on. רב פפא said: Why did our תנא leave out the איל נזיר, which is common, and use the איל המילואים instead?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's list of offerings whose bread is not made holy if slaughtered שלא לשמה. רב פפא is puzzled by the choice of example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איל נזיר also comes with bread, and it is brought all the time. The איל המילואים was brought only once, at the start of the משכן. So why teach the rare case and leave out the common one?

keyTerms.meaning: He left out
Our תנא, the author of our משנה
The ram a נזיר brings when he finishes his נזירות; it comes with bread
Common, happens often
The ram brought at the inauguration of the משכן

phrases.english: "If he slaughtered it not for its sake," etc.
Rav Pappa said:
Our Tanna left out
the nazir's ram, which is common,
and chose the ram of inauguration?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁבַק תַּנָּא דִידַן אֵיל נָזִיר דִּשְׁכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion on the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's choice of איל המילואים as its example
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה usually teaches the common case, and the איל נזיר is common while the איל המילואים happened only once.

steps.title: The משנה chose the original case
steps.stepSummary: Our תנא mentioned the איל המילואים because it is the main, original case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא picked the main, original case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב פפא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The איל המילואים was the first offering ever brought with bread. It is the root case, so the תנא used it as his example, even though the איל נזיר is more common.

keyTerms.meaning: The main or original matter
He chose or mentioned

phrases.english: And our Tanna
chose the main, original case.
phrases.notes: The איל המילואים was the first offering brought with bread, so it is the 'root' case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reason for the משנה's choice of example
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה should have used the common case, the איל נזיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה used the original, root case, the איל המילואים.

steps.title: משנה: נסכים made holy when the זבח turned out invalid
steps.stepSummary: If נסכים became holy in a כלי and the זבח was found פסול, they go with another זבח. If there is none, they become invalid by being left overnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the נסכים became holy in a service vessel, and then the offering was found to be invalid, here is the rule. If there is another offering, they should be brought with it. If not, they become invalid by being left overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with נסכים that were put in a holy כלי for an offering that turned out to be פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נסכים are already holy from the כלי, so they cannot just be used for anything. If another offering needs נסכים right now, they can go with it. If not, they are left overnight until they become פסול and are then burned.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה
The wine poured on the מזבח that goes along with an offering
A service vessel in the בית המקדש, which makes things holy
An offering that is invalid
Being left overnight, which makes holy items invalid

phrases.english: MISHNAH
The libations that became holy in a vessel
and the offering was found to be invalid,
if there is another offering,
they should be offered with it,
and if not,
they become invalid by being left overnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נסכים made holy in a כלי for a זבח פסול are brought with another זבח if there is one; otherwise they become פסול through לינה.

steps.title: זעירי: נסכים become holy only with the slaughter
steps.stepSummary: זעירי rules that נסכים become fully holy only when the זבח is slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: זעירי said: The נסכים become holy only when the offering is slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the משנה with a rule from זעירי about when נסכים become holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting the נסכים in a כלי is not enough by itself. They are tied to their offering, so they become fully holy only at the moment the זבח is slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא
Become holy
The slaughter of the offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule shows that the holiness of the נסכים depends on the זבח, which helps explain the משנה's case of a זבח פסול.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Ze'eiri said:
The libations do not become holy
except through the slaughter of the offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נסכים become holy only when the זבח is slaughtered.

steps.title: What is זעירי's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind זעירי's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where זעירי gets his rule from. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי's rule ties the holiness of the נסכים to the slaughter. The גמרא wants a source that shows this connection.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of step 20.

steps.title: The פסוק says 'זבח ונסכים'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק puts זבח and נסכים together, which shows the נסכים depend on the זבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'An offering and libations.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that links the נסכים to the זבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'זבח ונסכים' join the two together, so the נסכים go along with the זבח. That is why they become holy only when the זבח is slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering and libations, from the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: נסכים are tied to their זבח. According to זעירי, they become holy only when the זבח is slaughtered, as the פסוק says 'זבח ונסכים'.

phrases.english: The verse says:
"An offering and libations."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'זבח ונסכים' links the נסכים to the זבח, so they become holy only at its slaughter.

steps.title: The משנה about leftover נסכים seems to contradict זעירי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about נסכים whose זבח turned out פסול. It suggests the case is one where the זבח became פסול at its שחיטה, which would contradict זעירי.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: if נסכים became holy in a כלי and the זבח was found פסול, they go with another זבח if there is one. If not, they are disqualified by being left overnight. Isn't this talking about a זבח that became פסול at the שחיטה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the משנה from before, this time to attack זעירי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the זבח was פסול from its שחיטה, then by זעירי's rule the נסכים were never made fully holy. So why would they need לינה to become פסול? The משנה seems to show the כלי alone made them fully holy, against זעירי.

keyTerms.meaning: Became holy by being placed in a כלי שרת (a holy Temple vessel)
Becoming invalid by being left overnight
Isn't it so that...? (The גמרא suggests a reading that sets up a challenge)
Slaughtering the animal

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same משנה from step 19. The גמרא repeats it here for a new job: to use it as a challenge against זעירי.

phrases.english: We learned: the libations that became holy in a vessel
and the offering was found to be unfit –

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ זֶבַח אַחֵר, יִקְרְבוּ עִמּוֹ;
phrases.english: if there is another offering, they should be offered with it;
and if not – they become unfit by being left overnight.
Is it not where it became unfit through the slaughter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges זעירי's rule (steps 20-22) using the משנה from step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: זעירי's rule that נסכים become fully holy only at the שחיטה of the זבח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the זבח was פסול at שחיטה, the נסכים would not be fully holy under זעירי, yet the משנה requires לינה to disqualify them. That implies the כלי alone made them fully holy.

steps.title: No, the זבח became פסול only at the זריקה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge. The משנה is talking about a זבח that was slaughtered properly and only became פסול at the sprinkling of the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is talking about a זבח that became פסול at the זריקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and gives a different reading of the משנה that fits זעירי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שחיטה was valid, then by זעירי's rule the נסכים already became fully holy at that point. The problem with the זבח came only later, at the זריקה. So the נסכים really are fully holy, and they need לינה to become פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the blood of the קרבן on the מזבח
It became invalid

phrases.english: No, where it became unfit through the sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading behind the challenge in step 23
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the assumption that the משנה is about a זבח that was פסול at שחיטה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be about a valid שחיטה followed by a פסול זריקה. In that case the נסכים were already fully holy, even according to זעירי.

steps.title: Whose opinion does this answer follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא would agree that the נסכים became fully holy even though the זריקה was never done properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא the new reading of the משנה fits. It is setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both שחיטה and זריקה are things that make the נסכים permitted. If only the שחיטה was done properly, can the נסכים still be fully holy? That depends on a מחלוקת, so the גמרא asks whose view this follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Which תנא does this follow?

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks at what the answer in step 24 commits us to
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that נסכים are fully holy after only the שחיטה, without a valid זריקה

steps.title: It follows רבי: one of two מתירין is enough
steps.stepSummary: The answer fits רבי, who holds that when two things make something permitted, each one alone can raise it to holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like רבי, who said: two things that permit can each raise it to holiness, one without the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the reading in step 24 fits the view of רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שחיטה and the זריקה are the two מתירין for the נסכים. According to רבי, the שחיטה alone is enough to make the נסכים fully holy, even though the זריקה failed. This explains why the משנה requires לינה.

keyTerms.meaning: Two actions that make something permitted (here, שחיטה and זריקה)
Each one alone can raise it to holy status, even without the other

phrases.english: In accordance with Rabbi, who said:
two things that permit
elevate, this one without that one.
phrases.notes: Here that means the שחיטה alone makes the נסכים fully holy, even without a proper זריקה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי, who holds that one מתיר alone can make something fully holy

steps.title: It can even follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: the blood was collected and spilled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה can fit רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון too. The case is where the blood was collected in a cup and then spilled.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. Here we are talking about a case where he collected the blood in a cup and it spilled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to explain the משנה, so it does not have to follow only רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון disagrees with רבי and needs both מתירין. The גמרא changes the case: the blood was properly collected in a cup and was fit for זריקה, but then it spilled. In that situation, the נסכים were still made holy even according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say (you could even explain it according to...)
What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a specific case setup)
He collected their blood in a cup (a כלי שרת)
It spilled

steps.whatToRemember: זעירי survives: the משנה is about a זבח with a valid שחיטה. It fits רבי (one מתיר is enough), or even רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון if the blood was collected properly and then spilled.

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: Even if you say it is Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,
with what are we dealing here –
for example, where he collected their blood in a cup and it spilled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation so the משנה does not have to follow only רבי (step 26)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The answer in step 24 seemed to work only according to רבי
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה also fits רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, if the blood was collected in a cup, was fit for זריקה, and then spilled
